slot.brief: Pair like 'CAT : FDW', where each letter shifts by a constant; give a new word and ask for the analogous coded word using the same shift.

stem: In a certain code, PLAN is written as MOXQ. In the same code, how will SHIP be written?

verdicts.working: PLAN to MOXQ follows the pattern: P(-3)->M, L(+3)->O, A(-3)->X, N(+3)->Q. Applying this alternating -3, +3 shift to SHIP gives: S(-3)->P, H(+3)->K, I(-3)->F, P(+3)->S, resulting in PKFS.

working:
Compare PLAN with MOXQ letter by letter: P→M is −3, L→O is +3, A→X is −3, N→Q is +3. So the rule is that letters in odd positions shift back by 3 and letters in even positions shift forward by 3. Apply to SHIP: S(−3)=P, H(+3)=K, I(−3)=F, P(+3)=S. So SHIP is coded as PKFS, which is option A. Option B ends in R (P+2), C uses −2/+3/−2/+3 inconsistently (Q, K, G, S), D has J (H+2). Only A follows the alternating ±3 rule.

Independent check: PLAN to MOXQ follows the pattern: P(-3)->M, L(+3)->O, A(-3)->X, N(+3)->Q. Applying this alternating -3, +3 shift to SHIP gives: S(-3)->P, H(+3)->K, I(-3)->F, P(+3)->S, resulting in PKFS.
solution:
Compare PLAN with MOXQ: P→M (−3), L→O (+3), A→X (−3), N→Q (+3). Letters alternate between a shift of −3 and +3.
$$S(-3)=P,\; H(+3)=K,\; I(-3)=F,\; P(+3)=S$$
So SHIP is coded as PKFS, which is option (C).
